The Pinterest API significantly increases the scope of what is possible for you to create as a site or application developer. Access to the Pinterest API can be used for:

* Conversion tracking: Send conversion events.
* Content management: View, edit, delete Pins and boards.
* Ad management: View, edit, delete campaigns, ad groups, and ads.
* Media planning: Get campaign delivery estimates for reach, frequency, and other metrics.
* Targeting: View, edit, delete customer lists, audiences, trending keywords, and other targeting options.
* Shopping management: View, edit, delete catalog feeds and product groups.
* Analytics and reporting: Request analytics for your Pins, ads, ad groups, campaigns, or accounts.

In this reference, you will find information on all endpoints available in the Pinterest API. For implementation guides on supported use cases, visit our Docs page.

To get started with the Pinterest API and learn about what you need to do to authenticate, read this section of the API documentation. Alternatively, check out our development quickstart guide or Python SDK.

# Make an API call
Confirm whether you have access to the API by making a successful request.
First, ensure you've:
1. Completed the steps to [connect your app](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/connect-app/) and have been approved for access.
2. Recently created an [access token](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/set-up-authentication-and-authorization/#generate-an-access-token). If it's expired, you'll need to [refresh it](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/set-up-authentication-and-authorization/#refreshing-and-storing-tokens).
Use the following command to make a request to the [`pins/list`](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/api/v5/pins-list). This will return a list of pins in your account.
```bash
curl --location --request GET 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/pins' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR\_TOKEN' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
It should return a JSON response with a list of pins. If you have no pins, it will return an empty array, like so:
```json
{ "items": [], "bookmark": null }
```
\*\*Congratulations!\*\* You've made your first successful API call!

Pinterest works for all kinds of businesses, from small shops to global brands. It’s free to sign up for a business account and easy to start making Pins.

Work with one of our third-party partners to set up your feed, create shoppable experiences and more.

Take free courses and attend webinars from Pinterest marketing experts. On our free learning platform you’ll get tactical, in-depth training on campaign setup, creative best practices, optimization strategies and more.

Business accounts include additional features beyond standard Pinterest accounts. This includes special business tools like analytics and audience insights, plus access to Pinterest ads.

It’s free to sign up for a Pinterest business account. And if you decide to run ads, you can always set your own budget.

Application requests are reviewed by Pinterest. You will receive an email notification after your app has been reviewed, letting you know whether it was approved or denied access.

If your app is approved for Trial access, you can log into your account and manage your app details on your My apps page. In your My apps view, you'll be able to find details such as your unique app ID and app secret.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token

Python SDK: Our SDK currently offers a Python library that supports campaign management and simplifies authentication and error handling. Check it out here

Product limited tokens: Once your app is approved for Trial access you can generate a token to test the API without setting up the Oauth flow.Test tokens expire after 24 hours and allow you to explore certain endpoints faster.

The Pinterest API includes features that are in beta release as well as features that have restricted use. We identify these features with labels in the developer docs.

* Open beta features are available to all developers with access to the Pinterest API.
* Closed beta features are available to specific invited developers and organizations. In some cases, we also grant access by request.

If you try to call a restricted or closed beta endpoint without having been granted access by a Pinterest representative, you are likely to receive an error response indicating that you do not have access.
